clue.text: Cast get Russian names

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, so the letters of the next two words are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The actors in a play are all given Russian names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a troupe of actors but is the anagram signal, working on the ten letters of GET RUSSIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person's autograph is their name written by hand, so several autographs are names.

clue.text: Because of temperature, blue nose

parts.note: in can mean because of, as in 'in his haste he forgot the keys'
T is the physics abbreviation for temperature
blue means rude or risque, as in a blue joke

explanation.surface: The cold has turned somebody's nose blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nose' looks like the body part but is a verb here, meaning to pry or poke in where one is not wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to nose into someone's affairs is to pry or barge in uninvited.

clue.text: Brief direction — and not

indicators.note: brief means short, so the compass point loses its ending

parts.note: north is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A terse instruction, followed by a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary sense: the conjunction joins a second negative, as in 'neither this and not that'.

clue.text: Rules in place to cover circular letter writing

indicators.note: one piece covers the other by going round it on both sides

parts.note: there means in that place
the letter O is shaped like a circle
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Regulations exist to govern the sending of circulars.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'circular letter' reads as mass mail but is simply the round letter O, which 'to cover' puts inside THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: in mathematics a proven statement such as Pythagoras's serves as a rule.

clue.text: Jammed cylinder usually removed from steamer

definitions.text: Jammed cylinder usually removed from steamer

parts.words: Jammed cylinder usually removed from steamer
parts.note: it reads as a stuck engine part on a steamship, but describes a British suet dessert spread with jam, rolled into a log and cooked in a steamer

explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: this British suet dessert is spread with jam, rolled into a log shape and traditionally steamed.

clue.text: Divers get warm and use towel

parts.note: to sun oneself is to get warm in the sunshine
to dry is to use a towel after getting wet

explanation.surface: People who have been diving warm up and towel themselves down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like people plunging into water; it is the old adjective meaning various.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: divers is an archaic adjective meaning various or several.

clue.text: A lot of skill, but leaderless

indicators.note: without its leader, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: craft means skill, as in the craft of writing

explanation.surface: A group has plenty of talent but nobody in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a large number of things, as in a whole heap of new measures.

clue.text: Conversion of castle on rocky golden mile

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for the rook, also called the castle

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of the two words are shaken about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A castle beside a rocky stretch of seafront is being converted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Golden Mile is the seafront at Blackpool, an English resort; here 'rocky' rearranges GOLDEN MILE into EMODELLING, placed under R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: converting a building means reshaping and refitting it for a new use.

clue.text: Showing up of American in 18's address

indicators.note: in a down clue, showing up means the next word is written upwards
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the answer at 18 down is a verb meaning to cheat, as is con
US means American

explanation.surface: An American is exposed by the address of some numbered house.
explanation.walkthrough: The '18' is a cross-reference, not a house number: solve that clue first and take a short synonym of its answer. 'Showing up' and 'in' are the two indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to address a problem is to turn one's attention to it.

clue.text: Detailed subjects in rhyme

parts.note: detailed is read as de-tailed: the creatures in a nursery rhyme whose tails a farmer's wife cut off with a carving knife

explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: the sightless rodents of the nursery rhyme had their tails cut off, so they were de-tailed.

clue.text: One making the whole season

definitions.meaning: someone who adds figures up to make a total, whimsically
the warmest quarter of the year

explanation.definitionFit: One who adds up makes a total, and the same word names the warm part of the year.

clue.text: In earshot, PM splutters "I hate you all"

indicators.note: to splutter is to spit words out in disorder, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Within hearing, the Prime Minister spits out his loathing for everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splutters' rearranges IN EARSHOT PM; the quoted outburst is what such a person might say, standing for the person.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by speech: a hater of humankind is defined by what such a person would declare.

clue.text: Felicity is opening show

indicators.note: one word opens the other up by getting inside it

parts.note: a parade is a show or display
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actress called Felicity is the first act in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felicity' looks like a woman's name at the start of the clue but is the common noun for bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both words mean a state of perfect happiness or bliss.

clue.text: Full ownership of sub that's slow

parts.note: a sub is a subscription, a fee paid for membership
slow and simple both mean dim-witted

explanation.surface: Someone owns outright a submarine that is not very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal term: this is the absolute, unrestricted form of freehold title to land.

clue.text: Time to abandon factory proposal

indicators.note: one piece abandons the other, so it is taken away from it

parts.note: a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: The moment has come to drop the scheme for a new factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a scheme put forward for others to consider.

clue.text: Short people under fan

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: folk means people
lower can mean situated under, as in the lower deck

explanation.surface: Some small people are standing beneath a ceiling fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' looks like a position indicator but supplies letters itself; 'Short' trims FOLK to FOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a supporter or devotee of a team or star.

clue.text: George's son returned make-up

parts.note: S is the genealogy abbreviation for son

indicators.note: returned means the following piece comes back, written right to left

parts.note: DNA is a person's genetic make-up

explanation.surface: George's boy brought back the cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' is not cosmetics but genetic make-up, DNA, which 'returned' turns into AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the French novelist Amantine Dupin wrote under this pen name with George as the first name.

clue.text: United penetrating limits hapless spurs

indicators.note: one piece penetrates the other, going inside it
hapless means unlucky and all over the place, so the word's letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Manchester United break through against an unlucky Tottenham side.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs and United are English football clubs; 'hapless' rearranges LIMITS into STIMLI and 'penetrating' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a plural noun: things that goad or prompt a response.

clue.text: Weirdest place to house migrant workers

indicators.note: one piece houses the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a spot is a place
Okies were migrant farm workers from Oklahoma in 1930s America

explanation.surface: The strangest possible spot to accommodate travelling labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are superlatives meaning most eerie or uncanny.

clue.text: Take down leftovers, primarily to feed pigs

indicators.note: one piece is fed to the other, so it goes inside it

parts.note: swine are pigs

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Carry the leftover food downstairs, mainly to give to the pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take down' looks like one phrase; only 'Take' defines, in the slang sense of cheating someone, and 'down' gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: to take someone is to cheat or defraud them.

clue.text: Bill supporting prison in Cambridge

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: can is slang for prison
a tab is a bill, as in a bar tab

explanation.surface: A man called Bill backs a jail in Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation of the Latin Cantabrigiensis, written after a degree to show the university it was taken at.

clue.text: Picked up by inattentive boss, I cut in

indicators.note: the last word of the clue places the two middle pieces inside the boss

parts.note: MD is managing director, the boss of a British company
to shear is to cut, as with sheep's wool

explanation.surface: A careless manager took someone on, and I interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: something an inattentive listener picks up is caught wrongly by the ear.

clue.text: Power is turned on, finally accesses PC

parts.note: in mathematics a log, or logarithm, is the power to which a base is raised

indicators.note: turned means the word before it is written backwards
finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: The electricity comes on and at last someone can use the computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power' is mathematical, not electrical; 'turned' makes IS into SI and 'finally' takes the N of 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: entering a username and password is how one gains access to a computer.

clue.text: Late but worth waiting for

definitions.meaning: late means dead, no longer on this earth
something superb or heavenly is worth the wait

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes someone departed from earth and idiomatically something marvellous.

clue.text: When animals do it, it's habit

definitions.meaning: the annual mating season of deer and other animals
a fixed, dull routine one is stuck in

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the deer's mating season and a settled, tedious routine.

clue.text: Dutch partners provided parts

indicators.note: one piece parts the other, splitting it and sitting in the gap

parts.note: W and E, West and East, are partners at the bridge table
if means provided, as in 'provided it rains'

explanation.surface: Business partners from the Netherlands supplied components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is Cockney (London) slang for one's spouse, as in 'my old Dutch'; it is not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: in London slang a man's old Dutch is his spouse.

clue.text: Dictator from one country runs into trouble

indicators.note: the three short pieces go into the word for trouble

parts.note: bother means trouble
I is the Roman numeral for one
GB is Great Britain, a country
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A tyrant from a single nation finds himself in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the all-seeing ruler of Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, a byword for a tyrant.
